newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Cisneros eyes Banco Consolidado, oil.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Cisneros eyes Banco Consolidado, oil.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan businessman Oswaldo Cisneros, who holds Venezuela's Coca-Cola bottling concession, is considering diversifying his investments into Venezuelan oil and banking.
Cisneros told reporters at an oil conference in Caracas that he may team-up with the Sarmiento Group, owners of Banco de Bogota, to purchase state-owned Venezuelan bank Banco Consolidado.
"We're evaluating the bank to see its real worth," Cisneros told reporters at an oil conference in Caracas. "But it's an ideal size and well-recognised," he said.
Banco Consolidado, taken over by the Venezuelan government in 1994, is due to be sold at auction by the end of the year. Banco de Bogota is one of the 14 pre-qualified bidders.

Cisneros said he was also interested in possibilities in the oil industry, specifically the newly announced round of auctions for 20 marginal fields that makes preferential provisions for Venezuelan participation.
"We have the advantage of knowing the local scene well," he said.
Cisneros tried to diversify his interests into Venezuelan oil in the 1980s, but was barred by the government.
His brother Ricardo Cisneros is currently fugitive abroad facing charges of fraud and embezzlement for his role in the collapse of Banco Latino in 1994, of which he was a director.
